rationale: This is a cosmetic denominator tweak (removing `che` from `act+lct`) on the already-tested "Cash-Conversion-Floor Cash Discount," which shares the identical value leg, gate construction, and horizon, so it cannot produce substantively new evidence about the mechanism.

It differs from the archived "Current-Asset-Light Earnings Yield" only by swapping `ib`→`ni` and `act`→`act-che`, both minor perturbations of a specification whose long-short alpha was significantly the wrong sign, and the proposal offers no diagnosis of why that sign flip occurred.

The gate is simply the sign-flipped version of the already-tested noncash-current-asset drag term, and because the signed z-score dominates the [0,1] rank the composite mostly re-expresses the well-documented net-operating-asset/working-capital anomaly rather than a genuine value-interaction effect.

Subtracting `dp` from the numerator of the archived "Cost-Scaled Cash Conversion EBITDA Yield" gate is a marginal accounting adjustment to an otherwise identical expression, and the archive already contains a separate `oancf - dp` gate, so nothing new is being tested.

This is a mechanical re-pairing of an already-tested `NEG(dlc/lct)` gate with the most heavily reused value leg (`che`/market cap), and the stated economics — cash pre-committed to debt repayment — would be captured far more directly by a net-cash construction than by a multiplicative gate.

The pairing of an EV-based multiple with noncash operating-asset intensity is the least redundant item in this batch and has a coherent asset-light-versus-clogged-balance-sheet rationale, though it reuses a gate already tested elsewhere in the archive and its incremental content over that result is modest.
